title: Object.assign could add remote resource URLs to browser-created elements

reproduction.beforeFix: Direct, aliased and namespace-aware Object.assign calls returned pass, including an unknown source object that could contain an image URL.
reproduction.afterFix: The scanner resolves Object.assign targets and source property spreads, rejects statically remote resource values, and fails closed when a dynamic source may set a URL on an automatically loading resource element.

rootCause: The DOM resource mutation scanner handled setAttribute, Reflect.set, and Object.defineProperty, but did not inspect Object.assign target/source pairs.
remediation: Inspect Object.assign for resource-bearing DOM targets, recursively resolve static source objects and aliases, and reject uncertifiable source spreads for auto-loading tags.

validation.redBeforeFix: pnpm exec vitest run packages/registry-gate/src/__tests__/registry-gate.test.ts -t "remote resource mutations through Object.assign"
validation.redBeforeFixResult: failed as expected: direct Object.assign to an img passed before the fix; independent probes also passed for aliases, SVG image nodes, and unresolved props
validation.canonicalResourceIsolationMatrix: 324 resources passed, zero warnings, zero failures

runtimeBoundary: Static source analysis only; resource code was not executed. Preview CSP remains an independent network restriction. Release-candidate deployment verification remains pending.
